abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel information-theoretic framework for characterizing the fundamental limits of quantum-assisted communication systems operating over fading channels. Unlike conventional approaches that treat quantum and classical resources separately, we develop a unified capacity framework that jointly optimizes entanglement distribution and classical signal transmission under coherence-time constraints. By introducing the concept of quantum-classical duality regions, we derive closed-form expressions for the ergodic capacity and outage probability in Rayleigh fading environments. The proposed framework reveals that existing classical capacity bounds are loose by a factor of up to 3 dB when quantum receivers are employed. We further prove that superposition coding with quantum successive interference cancellation achieves the capacity region of the quantum multiple access channel with fading. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed paradigm enables throughput gains exceeding 40% compared to state-of-the-art quantum communication protocols. This work fundamentally reshapes our understanding of the interplay between quantum resources and wireless propagation effects, providing new design criteria for next-generation communication systems that leverage quantum advantages in practical fading scenarios.

This paper presents a rigorous theoretical analysis of iterative detection algorithms for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems under imperfect channel state information. We derive novel bounds on the convergence rate of message-passing algorithms by characterizing the coupling between channel estimation errors and detection performance. The key innovation lies in developing a perturbed loopy belief propagation framework that accounts for both hardware impairments and channel estimation uncertainty. We prove that the proposed detector achieves a diversity order of min(N_t, K) with only O(K log K) complexity, where N_t is the number of transmit antennas and K is the number of users. Our analysis reveals that existing MMSE-based detectors suffer from a 2 dB SNR penalty due to residual channel estimation errors, which can be eliminated through the proposed interference-aware detection scheme. Furthermore, we derive tight approximations for the bit error rate that are valid for arbitrary antenna configurations. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm approaches the theoretical bound within 0.5 dB for systems with up to 128 antennas. This work provides rigorous design guidelines for implementing practical massive MIMO receivers in frequency-selective fading environments.

This paper presents a revolutionary reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-empowered terahertz communication architecture for ultra-massive MIMO satellite systems. Unlike conventional RIS designs that assume passive reflection, we introduce an actively-controlled RIS architecture with integrated sensing capabilities that enables simultaneous beamforming and environmental awareness. The proposed system employs a hierarchical codebook design that adapts to dynamic atmospheric conditions and satellite mobility patterns. We develop a novel joint active-passive beamforming algorithm that maximizes the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio while minimizing the communication latency for satellite-to-ground links. The hardware architecture incorporates novel graphene-based phase shifters that achieve 360-degree continuous phase control with sub-millisecond switching times. Field trials in the 140 GHz band demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves aggregate data rates exceeding 1 Tbps with latencies below 10 ms, representing a tenfold improvement over existing satellite communication systems. The system seamlessly integrates with existing 5G non-terrestrial network protocols, enabling transparent handover between terrestrial and satellite segments. This paradigm shift enables unprecedented connectivity for maritime, aviation, and disaster-resilient communication scenarios.

This paper proposes a novel underwater acoustic communication system that leverages deep learning-based adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) for robust data transmission in highly dynamic ocean environments. The system architecture incorporates a long short-term memory (LSTM) network that predicts channel state evolution and adaptively selects modulation orders and coding rates in real-time. We implement the system on a heterogeneous underwater sensor network testbed comprising vertical line arrays and autonomous underwater vehicles. The proposed algorithm reduces packet error rates by 60% compared to conventional AMC approaches while maintaining spectral efficiency within 1 dB of the theoretical optimum. The hardware prototype operates in the 9-34 kHz frequency band with adaptive bandwidth allocation from 4 kHz to 16 kHz based on channel conditions. Experimental results collected during a 72-hour sea trial demonstrate that the system achieves reliable communication ranges up to 10 km with data rates ranging from 1 kbps to 40 kbps. The proposed design significantly advances underwater communications for ocean monitoring, underwater robotics, and maritime emergency response applications.
